Beam bending calculator

Deflection curve, slopes, stiffness and bending stress for standard support and load cases.

How it works

Euler–Bernoulli beam theory: the curvature of a beam equals M/(E·I). Integrating twice and applying the support conditions gives the deflection curve, slopes and stiffness for each load case.

Key points

  • Stiffness scales with E·I/L³, so length matters most. Halving L gives an 8× stiffer beam.
  • Clamped ends are much stiffer than pinned ends. For a central load, clamped–clamped is 4× stiffer than simply supported.
  • The maximum stress is at the point of maximum moment, at the outer fibre: σ = M·e/I.
  • Self-weight is a uniform load q = ρ·g·A.

Assumptions

  • Slender beam: L/h > 10 (shear deformation neglected)
  • Small slopes (< 5°)
  • Linear elastic
